members.title: Removing the Math.min(100, ...) clamp brings back over-100% progress for extracted files (undoes fix 879266c)
members.problem: This diff removes the clamp that commit 879266c added to fix a bug found during the v1.4.0 walkthrough. An extracted file's localSize is the unpacked size and its remoteSize is the compressed archive size, so localSize/remoteSize goes above 1. With the clamp gone, an extracted file with local=20 and remote=10 now gets percentDownloaded=200. Effects in transfer-row.component.html: line 28 shows '200%'; line 33 success class is false; line 53 ETA shows '-' instead of 'Done'. Only the bar width at line 35 still clamps.
members.why_it_matters: It reintroduces a user-visible defect that was already fixed and shipped (wrong '199%'-style labels, missing success state, missing 'Done' text) on every extracted transfer.
members.fix_hint: Put back Math.min(100, Math.trunc(100.0 * localSize / remoteSize)) and the comment explaining it, unless showing more than 100% is an intended product change. If it is intended, update the ===100 checks in transfer-row.component.html and the spec vectors to match.

members.title: Removed clamp brings back progress values above 100% for extracted files
members.problem: The diff removes Math.min(100, ...) from percentDownloaded. The deleted comment says why the clamp was there: an extracted file has a local_size bigger than its remote_size (the unpacked files are larger than the compressed archive), so localSize/remoteSize goes above 1 and the UI shows values like '199%'. The diff adds no other bound, so any extracted file whose local_size is larger than its remote_size now gets a percentDownloaded over 100.
members.why_it_matters: Users will see impossible values like '199%' downloaded. Progress bars or width styles that take this value can also overflow. This brings back a bug that was already fixed and documented.

members.title: Reverts the single place that clamps percentDownloaded, leaving consumers that assume 0-100 with values above 100
members.problem: Commit 879266c made view-file.service.ts the one place that normalizes percentDownloaded to 0-100, because extracted files have localSize (unpacked) larger than remoteSize (archive). This diff removes that clamp and its comment. transfer-row.component.html is the only consumer, and only its width binding (line 35) clamps. The displayed text at line 28 now shows values like '199%'. The === 100 checks for the success style (line 33) and the 'Done' ETA label (line 53) silently fail for every extracted file, so finished extractions look unfinished.
members.why_it_matters: The ViewFile model is the contract between the service and the views. Removing the clamp pushes range handling onto every consumer. The current template handles it for the bar width only, which brings back a user-visible bug that was fixed and tested in v1.4.x.
members.fix_hint: restore Math.min(100, ...) at the source (and its explanatory comment); if uncapped ratio is needed for a new feature, expose it as a separate ViewFile field rather than changing the semantics of percentDownloaded

findings.title: Existing unit test vectors expect the clamp and will fail (CI break)
findings.problem: The test 'should correctly set ViewFile percent downloaded' has the vectors [20, 10, 100] and [100, 50, 100]. The unclamped code returns 200 for both, so expect(file!.percentDownloaded).toBe(testVectors[count][2]) fails twice. The diff changes only the service and leaves the spec untouched.
findings.fix_hint: Put the clamp back (preferred). If over-100% is now intended, update these vectors in the same change.
findings.why_it_matters: The Angular unit test suite goes red, which blocks CI and release.
